name: Schools Out For Summer

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline, opening the promotion's first international pay-per-view, taped at Wembley Stadium, London.

matches.note: Crucafix's CROW debut; won by pinfall with the Crucifixion after Guyver turned his back on him.
CROW International Championship. The Destroyer's ringside interference, meant for Rob the Rock, struck champion Alex Nelson instead; Rob the Rock won the title with the Brooklyn Bomb.

CROW Light Heavyweight Championship battle royal, also drawing Mad Goat, Jawbreaker, Pakradja, Guyver, Reverend JJ and Crucafix; not preserved in full in the surviving broadcast text, but the broadcast's own later commentary credits Smoke with the win after Travis Smith's debut mistakes, becoming the new champion.
Hard-core rules #1 contenders match for the CROW Tag Team Championship. Smoke and Who Else (Death and Destruction) won by pinfall at 38:48 after the Hellbound Drop.
Vacant CROW Television Championship. “DD” Derek Douglas won by pinfall with the Flatliner at 28:58.
Shawn Jamison won by pinfall at 24:07 over the visiting HVD wrestler Jawbreaker.
King of Kings cage match (billed as for CROW ranking, not a title). The Destroyer won by escaping the cage at 38:07, with Mr. Menace striking Master Ito during the match.

evidence.source: the promotion's own 'Schools Out For Summer' broadcast
evidence.note: An eight-match card headlined by a non-title cage match, with two title changes (International, Television) and a third title decided by an unpreserved battle-royal segment.

notes: The Light Heavyweight battle royal's own play-by-play does not survive among the posts recovered; its result is recorded from the broadcast's own subsequent on-air commentary.

name: Scorch Wave 98

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline, taped at the Tokyo Skydome, Japan; advertised beforehand under the working title 'Heat Wave'.

matches.note: Casket match. The Destroyer won at 26:25.
Wildcat cage match. Beefcarver won at 18:52.
Three-way #1 contender's match for the CROW Light Heavyweight Championship, won by pinfall by Giant Leopard at 28:56.
Texas Death Match. Steve Houston won at 23:37, becoming #1 contender for the CROW International Championship.
Loser-leaves-CROW tag match. Death and Destruction won by pinfall at 5:44; the Dark Riders left the promotion.
CROW Tag Team Championship. Element Of Pain won by pinfall at 27:52 with the Destroyer's ringside interference, ending the Gospel Preachers' reign.
CROW International Championship, ladder match. Rob the Rock retained at 18:23.
#1 contender's match for the CROW World Heavyweight Championship. Derek Douglas won by pinfall at 20:47, then announced a new stable, the Devils Children, with Shane Alexander and Beefcarver.
Declared a draw by double count-out at 16:48.
Loser-leaves-CROW match. Snake Master won by pinfall at 14:06; Elvis Maloney left the promotion, and Snake Master announced his own retirement as a broadcaster.
CROW World Heavyweight Championship, 2-out-of-3-falls falls-count-anywhere main event. King Dare won 2 falls to 1, becoming the new champion.

evidence.note: An eleven-match, four-hour card with three title changes (Tag Team, World Heavyweight, and a contested Light Heavyweight result) plus a #1 contenders' scramble whose own team lineup the surviving text does not resolve cleanly, left uncounted here.

evidence.source: the promotion's own 'Scorch Wave 98 Post PPV: Update'
evidence.note: Narrates the promotion's own mid-year merger into a planned four-federation alliance and a separate, unconfirmed plan to decide the Light Heavyweight title on another federation's card.

notes: The broadcast's own closing recap credits Giant Leopard as the new Light Heavyweight Champion, while the promotion's own same-day post-PPV update instead describes the title as stripped and pending a decider match on another federation's card; the promotion's own next surviving ranking sheet (28 October) shows Levi Ash holding the title, and no surviving document reconciles the two accounts. An additional scramble (Da Gang vs. the Replacement Killers, billed as a #1 contenders tag match) ended in a double disqualification; its own team lineup is not resolved clearly enough in the surviving text to structure as a match.

name: CROW Contract Match (card sample)

date.source: A sample match posted with the hiring call of 2 May 2002; it carries no date of its own.

notes: Posted as a sample of the match writing the reopened promotion would run.
